name: Fairmont Orchid
positioning: Fairmont Orchid, Hawaiʻi: an oceanfront resort on the Big Island's Kohala Coast with a private lagoon, an open-air spa and Hawaiian cultural activities
best_for: Travelers who want a beach resort with snorkeling and Hawaiian cultural activities
Guests who like an open-air spa and a Fairmont Gold lounge option

facts.text: The resort sits on the Big Island's Kohala Coast.
Rooms and suites have private lanais, which are verandas, with ocean or garden views.
The resort has an open-air spa called Spa Without Walls.
The resort offers cultural activities including hula, lei making and storytelling.
Brown's Beach House focuses on fish dishes and has a kids menu.
Binchotan Bar & Grill has a 14-seat sushi bar.
The Fairmont Gold Lounge has an outdoor lanai with resort and ocean views.
The resort has wheelchair accessible rooms with grab bars and visual alarms.
Guests can play 18 holes at Mauna Lani Golf Club.

highlights.text: Guests can watch the sunrise from an outrigger canoe on Pauoa Bay with the resort's navigator, called the hoʻokele.
Guests can snorkel in the resort's private lagoon.
The resort holds the Hawaii Loa Luau on Friday nights.
Fairmont Gold guests are escorted to a private reception area on the 6th floor of the North Tower.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes the remote Kohala Coast location requires a car or resort shuttle for off-property dining and exploration.
Golf is played at Mauna Lani Golf Club.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing may not suit all budgets.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont Orchid Hawaii
